questions.q: What did the research on commercial gender-classification products find?
options: Error rates differed noticeably between subgroups, revealing bias
All three products were equally accurate for every group
The products failed mainly because the images were low resolution
Accuracy was poor for every subgroup alike
questions.explain: Overall accuracy looked good, but misgendering was higher for women and for people with darker skin.
questions.evidence: there was a noticeable difference in error rates between various subgroups

questions.q: Which lesson did that facial-analysis research draw for data science?
options: It should stop using images of people altogether
It needs bigger GPUs to remove bias
Bias can only be fixed after a product is released
It needs more representative datasets and more inclusive teams
questions.explain: Balanced subgroups and diverse teams help catch bias earlier in AI solutions.
questions.evidence: data science needs more representative datasets (balanced subgroups) and more inclusive teams (diverse backgrounds)

questions.q: How does UPS use data science, according to the lesson?
options: To correlate search terms with flu trends
To visualise a day in the life of New York taxis
To predict optimal delivery routes using weather, traffic and deadlines
questions.explain: Route prediction takes weather, traffic patterns and delivery deadlines into account.
questions.evidence: UPS uses data science and machine learning to predict optimal routes for delivery
